issues.description: Format B assumes metrics is a dict; truthy non-dict metrics crashes ingestion with AttributeError instead of warning and skipping.
Format C does not catch XML ParseError, so one malformed XML file aborts the entire ingest.
NaN scores are accepted by parsing and bypass clamp comparisons, causing invalid data or SQLite IntegrityError during ingest.
The CLI checks for zero discovered files only after ingest mutates the database, so an error path can create or alter a DB.
Empty ingests still connect, create schema, clear warnings, and reset stats before the CLI reports failure.
Blank or null run IDs are accepted, which can silently overwrite rows under the UNIQUE(run_id, source) constraint.
CSV over-split recovery treats every row with more than six fields as unquoted-meta recovery, masking structurally malformed rows.
CSV and JSONL parsers read whole files into memory instead of streaming, which is fragile for large evaluation outputs.
XML parsing uses stdlib ElementTree directly on input files with no hardened parser or file-size guard.
Project metadata does not declare test dependencies or optional dev extras, so a fresh contributor install cannot run tests from metadata alone.
